thought.text: The `pkill` is matching my own shell (the command line contains the pattern). Let me use a bracket pattern to avoid self-match and relaunch.

reasoning_content: pkill keeps matching the parent shell (the terminal's `bash -lc` wrapper command line contains the pattern). Let me use a more targeted approach to kill the app: kill by the exact nx executor child pids, or use a pattern that won't match the shell. Actually the issue: my shell command line literally contains "sva-studio-react:serve" (in the pkill argument), so `pkill -f` matches the shell itself → exit 143 (killed). I need to avoid self-match. Use `pkill -f 'run sva-studio-react:serve'`? That still appears in my command. Better: find the pids and kill by pid, excluding my own shell. Or use a pattern with a character class trick: `pkill -f 'sva-studio-react:ser[v]'` — the bracket prevents matching the literal string in my own command line.

action.command:
cd /workspace && pkill -f 'sva-studio-react:ser[v]e' 2>/dev/null; pkill -f 'run-executor.[j]s' 2>/dev/null; sleep 3
echo "app procs: $(ps -eo pid,args | grep -c '[s]va-studio-react:serve')"
nohup pnpm exec tsx /tmp/launch-app2.mjs > /tmp/launch11.log 2>&1 & sleep 4; cat /tmp/launch11.log
